spec_match.rationale: Implements the explainer's Example 1 (table with labels on top and left) with the real mechanism: position:sticky top/left cells inside a wrapper whose overflow mode toggles between scroll clip, scroll hidden, and bare overflow-x:auto, exposing the per-axis sticky-ancestor rule.

interactive.rationale: Mode radios restyle the live wrapper; the jump button scrolls the page and the wrapper; the header-state readout recomputes stuck/not-stuck from getBoundingClientRect on every page and wrapper scroll.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The blurb promises top labels riding the page scroll and left labels riding the wrapper's horizontal scroll, possible only with an x-axis-only container — the page demonstrates and measures exactly that claim.

edge_cases.rationale: Includes the subtle classic trap (bare overflow-x:auto silently coercing overflow-y to auto) alongside the legacy scroll hidden workaround, and the readout explains that a wrapper with nothing to scroll vertically is still a vertical scroll container for sticky purposes.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/5067363861004288, the spec section, the explainer's Example 1, and csswg issue 8286 where the sticky problem was resolved.

conformance.rationale: The suite's computed-value discriminators cover the wrapper contract this page depends on; the sticky-anchor consequence itself is demonstrated live and mirrored in the mode readout rather than asserted, since it needs page-scroll interaction.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: jump scrolled the page to 1527px, header honestly reported NOT stuck (header −296px riding wrapper −298px), mode readout showed the dual-axis classification, sticky left week labels visibly pinned during scrollLeft=180 in the screenshot, console clean. The header-pins-to-viewport branch needs Chrome 152+.

telemetry_health.rationale: sasc-sticky-single-axis-wrapper fires only when the wrapper genuinely computes overflow-y: clip; coerced browsers report the separate sasc-sticky-dual-axis-fallback id.

design_system.rationale: Header row is text-black background with bg-ivory text (AA), row labels bg-stone with text-black, readout accents via variables; sticky cells carry explicit backgrounds so content never shows through.

accessibility.rationale: Real table semantics with scoped th for both axes, the wrapper is a keyboard-focusable labelled region, mode radios are native inputs in a legended fieldset with 44px rows, and both readouts are role=status aria-live=polite text equivalents of the sticky state.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×1600: table scrolls horizontally inside the wrapper with no page-level overflow on either class, controls stack cleanly, tap targets ≥44px; console clean apart from the environmental fonts.googleapis failure.

openQuestions.title: Record the viewport-pinned header on a supporting browser
openQuestions.detail: On Chrome 152+ in scroll clip mode, scroll past the wrapper top and verify the header-state readout flips to STUCK with the header holding near 0px while the wrapper top goes negative, and that switching to scroll hidden makes it ride away again; refresh runtime_evidence with that capture.

openQuestions.title: Consider a scrollIntoView-into-table variant for DOM scroll APIs on the clip axis
openQuestions.detail: The explainer also calls out scrollIntoView within single-axis tables; a small addition could focus a cell and show the page (not the wrapper) handling the vertical adjustment when the wrapper is x-axis-only.

guidanceConsulted.query: sticky table header column position sticky scroll container
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep wide tables scrollable in a dedicated container and preserve native table semantics rather than rebuilding with divs.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The demo uses a real table with scoped row/column th elements inside the single wrapper under test; wide content scrolls in the wrapper so the page never overflows horizontally.

guidanceConsulted.query: scroll position aware sticky header state
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Derive scrolled-state UI from actual scroll geometry rather than assumptions, throttling with rAF.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The header-state readout computes stuck/not-stuck from live getBoundingClientRect comparisons in a requestAnimationFrame-throttled scroll listener on both the window and the wrapper.

summary: The sticky-per-axis flagship demo: three wrapper modes over one real table, with a measured header-state readout proving whose scroll the top labels anchor to. On sandbox Chromium 141 it demonstrates and honestly labels the legacy failure (header rides the wrapper away); the left-label stickiness against the wrapper's horizontal scroll is verified working in both eras.
